properties.statement: A SIDEWAYS FINDING, so nothing else will record it. 2026-09-06: two full `cargo test -p reflow2-mcp` runs were started overlapping (one launched before the other finished). In that run, the_sync_roll_is_bounded_and_says_so.rs::a_seat_that_accumulated_records_opens_a_bounded_number_and_names_the_rest FAILED at its 'every record is either opened or NAMED' assertion (line ~87). Re-run ALONE, the same test passed in 0.01 s; the full suite run alone that followed passed 358/358 and later 366/366. No code the failing test exercises had changed between the runs. So the failure correlates with CONCURRENT suite processes, not with the code under test. NOT ESTABLISHED (candidates, unmeasured): the test may read or write a shared path (a temp dir keyed on something not process-unique, or the real .reflow2 sidecar), or it may count records under a time window that a slow, contended machine violates. WHY IT IS WORTH A NODE: a later session that sees this test fail once will otherwise root-cause a phantom in the sync roll. The first check is 'was another cargo test running?' — and the habit to keep is one suite run at a time, sequentially, which is also what every honest measurement this week needed.
